- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to underpredict sharp upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for the next 3–5 days.
- After a spike in price (e.g., >15% from prior peak), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast at +10% above peak for next 5 days.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-period, model lags in recognizing momentum; add 1–3 days of upward bias in forecast.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizons when sentiment is mixed or neutral; reduce forecast volatility by 10–20% in middle-range days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates true volatility in high-sentiment periods; add 5–10% upward bias if sentiment > 0.5 for 3+ consecutive days.
- If true outcome shows “reversal after spike” (e.g., spike then drop), model often fails to anticipate; add 1–2 days of downward bias after peak.
